what_happened: The route said turn right and the recorded path did, but the ego kept going straight and drifted left to straddle the lane line. That put it behind a slower white sedan (actor 99) in the left lane. The gap fell from 34 m to 0.5 m while the ego only eased from 13 to 10 m/s, and its front-left hit the sedan's rear.

On a narrow residential street lined with parked cars, the ego drove at about 13–14 m/s and drifted about 1.8 m left of the human's path into the left parking lane. Its front struck parked car 6 at the left kerb at 7.1 s. The gap to that car shrank from 32 m to 1.6 m while the ego slowed only slightly (14.6 to 12.3 m/s).

The route said RIGHT, but the ego drove straight through the intersection at about 10.5 m/s and didn't follow the recorded right turn (it ended up 26 m from the recording). Past the intersection it stayed toward the left and drifted over the left lane edge onto the median/tram-stop area, which counts as offroad at 9.7 s. The camera smeared on the right side only after the ego had already moved away from the recorded path, so it doesn't explain the mistake.

At an intersection where the route turns right, the ego drove at about 6 m/s and its planned path bent left instead of following the right-turn route. At 6.2 s it was flagged offroad while only 0.8 m from the human's recorded path, and no front or side collision appears in the frames.

The route command was RIGHT, but the policy turned left at about 3.5 m/s, away from the recorded path (7.3 m off it). It drove head-on into van 155, which was coming the other way in that street. The ego never slowed while the gap shrank from 10 m to 3.8 m, and the front collision happened at 9.0 s.

On a narrow residential street lined with parked cars, the ego kept going about 12–14 m/s and drifted left toward the parked-car lane instead of keeping right ahead of the right turn it had been told to make. It barely slowed as the gap closed (32 m to 1.6 m) and hit parked car 6 head-on at about 12 m/s; it was also flagged offroad.

The ego was in a right-turn lane, and the route bent right through the intersection, but the policy planned straight and to the left (the orange path). It steered left out of the turn lane and was flagged offroad at 6.2 s, about 0.8 m from the recorded path, with no lead vehicle close by. The collision metrics stay at 0 in every frame, so the failure is the offroad. The camera view looks clean until then, and the command showed STRAIGHT until the last frame, which may have added to the confusion.

The route turned right at the intersection, but after handoff at about 4.7 s the policy planned a path that veered left, the opposite way. At about 4.5 m/s the ego drifted left of its lane at the stop line and was flagged offroad at 6.2 s, only 0.7 m from the recorded human path. No other actor was involved, and the camera view looked clean beforehand.

The ego was approaching a signalized intersection on a green light with no one close ahead (the nearest vehicle was about 30 m away). Its route turned right, but after the policy took over at 4.7 s its planned path swung left. At 6.2 s the ego drifted left out of its lane and was flagged offroad. The collision metrics in the frames stay at 0, so the offroad is the real failure.

At about 3.5–3.9 m/s in the intersection, the ego left the planned route, which continues straight up the street ahead, and turned sharply left toward the left-hand street. It clipped the corner and went off the road at the building and the parked car (the camera at 9.0s faces the Dinkelacker storefront), 4.2 m from the recorded human path. No actor was involved; the camera views before the failure look clean.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded path went straight/right through the intersection, but after handoff the ego turned left into the narrow side street. It kept speeding up (about 3.1 to 3.8 m/s) as the gap shrank from 10 m to 4 m, and its front hit the white van (actor 155) sitting in that street's lane, facing the ego. A rear contact is also flagged, but the front collision is the failure; it happened mid-turn on a path the policy chose against the command.

While turning through the intersection, the ego left the recorded path (about 7 m off) and steered into the lane of white van 155, which was coming toward it. The van was clearly visible on camera. The ego kept speeding up as the gap closed from 10 m to 4 m and hit the van head-on at about 3.5 m/s. The rear contact came later.

After handoff, the ego drove at about 13–14 m/s along the left edge of a narrow residential street, over the dashed lane line next to the row of parked cars, instead of following the route on the right. It kept heading straight at parked car 6 in its path, closing the gap from 32 m to 1.5 m while slowing only to 12.3 m/s, and hit it with its front.

After handoff (4.7s), the route called for a right turn at the intersection, but the policy's planned path (orange) bent left, away from the route. At about 6 m/s the ego drifted out of its lane and was flagged offroad at 6.2s. No vehicle was close ahead (gap over 30 m), and the frames show no front collision: collision metrics read 0, even though the input says collision_at_fault, and the box behind the ego at 6.2s fits the rear-ended flag.

The route command was RIGHT and the route line ran north-east through the intersection, but at about 3 m/s the ego swung left toward the parked cars on the west street. Its front hit vehicle 12, which was turning into that same street.

The ego was approaching a signalized intersection at about 4.4 m/s, with the route turning right. The command read STRAIGHT until the last frame, and the policy's plan swung left and straight instead of following the right turn. At 6.2 s, near the stop line, the offroad flag fired while the ego was only 0.7 m from the human's recorded path and still looked to be inside the mapped lane, so this is probably a marginal map-boundary hit rather than a clear drift off the road.

The route command was RIGHT, but the ego turned left across the intersection, about 6.4 m off the recorded path. At about 3.2 m/s it drove its front into the white van (actor 155) facing it in the side street, while the gap shrank from 11 m to 4.9 m. The camera view is clean before impact, so rendering does not explain the error; the rear contact came after the front collision.

The route said turn right, but the ego crept into the intersection at about 2.5 m/s and steered left, ending 3.2 m off the recorded path. That put it in the path of an oncoming car (actor 12, the dark sedan) turning across the intersection, and the ego hit it with its front-left corner without stopping.

After handoff, the ego drifted left out of the rightmost lane into the next lane, where the slower actor 2 was driving. It held about 12 m/s and hit actor 2 from behind with its front. The recorded path stayed in the right lane, and the command at the failure was RIGHT.

The route said RIGHT, but the ego turned left across the intersection into the narrow street with parked cars, about 6.4 m off the recorded path. Holding about 3.5 m/s without braking, it drove its front into the white van (actor 155) facing it in that lane; the gap to the van closed from 9.1 m to 5.1 m.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded path went straight across the intersection, but the policy turned left toward the cross street. Its planned path cut through the row of vehicles there (155/101), and at about 3.8 m/s the front of the ego hit a white van facing it (likely actor 155). The rear contact flagged in the run happened only after this front collision.

On a RIGHT command at the intersection, the ego turned too tightly at about 3.5 m/s. Its planned path ran toward the curb, and its front hit a car parked along the right side (actor 90), about 8 m off the recorded trajectory. Car 112, which was crossing behind it, then touched the ego's rear, but only after the front collision had started.

After handoff the ego kept going about 12 m/s and steered left out of its curb-side lane into the next lane. That lane held slower car 2, and the ego ran into its rear (front collision at 6.7 s) without slowing; the route and the recorded path stayed to the right.

With a RIGHT command, the ego drove up the left side of the street next to the row of parked cars instead of moving toward the right-turn lane. It kept speeding up to about 7.5–7.9 m/s while the gap to parked car 6 ahead fell from 18 m to 3 m, never braked or steered away, and its front hit the parked car at 9.1 s.

The route turns right at the intersection, but the policy's planned path (orange) swung left toward the tram tracks. Just after handoff, the ego drifted left at about 6 m/s and crossed the left edge of the drivable area. It was only 0.8 m from the recorded human path, and nothing was nearby (the lead car was more than 30 m ahead). The route command showed STRAIGHT until the last frame, which may have added to the confusion, but it never pointed left.
